idiom_name: shared frozen no-op object + optional chaining (?., ??)
implementation_notes: JavaScript has no interfaces and no compile-time null checking, so the classic abstract-base/null-subclass structure collapses into two idioms: a single shared object whose methods do nothing (const nullLogger = Object.freeze({ log() {} })) used as a constructor default, and optional chaining with a default (logger?.log(msg)) where absence may still matter. The shared object is the null object proper - callers keep one call syntax and drop the guards - while ?. and ?? (ES2020) cover the remaining nullable references. Duck typing means the null object only has to implement the members callers actually use, so keep it next to the interface it stands in for.
pitfalls: ?? and || differ: || also replaces valid falsy values (0, '', false), so a default written with || silently swallows legitimate configuration.
Optional chaining only guards the link it is applied to - a?.b.c still throws when b is null - and the undefined it returns is easily mistaken for a null object that did its job.
Sharing a mutable no-op object leaks state between callers, and Object.freeze is shallow; define the null object as a frozen (or module-level singleton) object and never store per-call data on it.
